short_statement: A general saturation formula now describes stability beyond phase-type service. The remaining challenge is computing its threshold with certified accuracy and useful complexity guarantees.
full_statement:
There are $N$ identical servers and one FCFS queue. Arrivals form a renewal process with iid positive interarrival times of mean $1/\lambda$. Independently, jobs have iid joint marks $(B,S)$, where $B\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is the number of simultaneously required servers and $S>0$ is the duration, with $\mathbb E S<\infty$. Dependence between a job's size $B$ and duration $S$ is allowed. A job occupies all $B$ servers for its entire service; a blocked head-of-line job prevents later jobs from starting.

The saturated workload construction makes all jobs available at time zero. For a sorted vector $h\in\mathbb R_+^N$, define $T_b(h)_i=\max(h_b,h_i)$ and $(e_b)_i=\mathbf1\{i\le b\}$. Starting at $H_0=0$, set
$$H_{n+1}=\operatorname{sort}\bigl(T_{B_n}(H_n)+S_n e_{B_n}\bigr),\qquad \gamma=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\max_i H_{n,i}}{n}.$$
The monotone-separable saturation rule gives a finite stationary workload below the threshold $\lambda_c=1/\gamma$. The equality case $\lambda=\lambda_c$ needs separate analysis.

The remaining open problem is effective computation of $\gamma$, not existence of a general threshold representation. For example, given rational finite-support job marks, $N$, and rational $\delta,\eta\in(0,1)$, construct certified bounds $\gamma_-\le\gamma\le\gamma_+$ of width at most $\delta$ (deterministically, or with probability at least $1-\eta$), and quantify runtime in the input bit length, $N$, $\delta^{-1}$, and $\log(1/\eta)$. Can this be done without enumerating an exponentially large saturated state space, or is there a complexity obstruction? State any support, moment, or separation assumptions needed for the algorithm.
known_results:
Wang, Xie, and Harchol-Balter emphasize that even the exact stability region is very hard, and they derive sufficient conditions for zero queueing in large-system scaling regimes. Grosof, Harchol-Balter, and Scheller-Wolf give a closed-form stability region for the two-class FCFS multiserver-job system with distinct server requirements and exponential service distributions. Grosof, Hong, Harchol-Balter, and Scheller-Wolf (Performance Evaluation 162, 2023, article 102378), Sections 2.2 and 3, describe the saturation-rule criterion for Poisson arrivals with i.i.d. joint server-need/phase-type-duration marks. Appendix C computes the threshold from finite balance equations. Theorem 4.2 further gives mean response time to additive $O(1)$ as arrival rate approaches that threshold. Thus exact finite-state characterization extends beyond two classes. This is not a polynomial-in-input-size complexity theorem.

Baccelli, Olliaro, Ajmone Marsan, and Marin (arXiv:2601.20653v1, 2026), Theorems 4.2 and 5.1, establish a monotone-separable workload recursion and the pile-growth threshold for general finite-mean service durations, including the iid marked renewal model above. Section 5 explicitly leaves the complexity of evaluating $\gamma$ open. Algorithm 2 estimates the limit numerically; successive estimates becoming close are not a certified error bound. Likewise, their sub-perfect sampling procedure returns lower approximations, not an observable certificate of an exact stationary sample.

Remaining open problem. Obtain compact or complexity-controlled, certified evaluation of the threshold. Do not describe general non-phase-type threshold existence as still wholly open.

progress.summary: A 2026 preprint extends the saturation representation to general service durations. Finite-state phase-type methods remain available; certified efficient evaluation of the general pile-growth constant is unresolved.

literature.synthesis: The 2023 phase-type analysis and the 2026 workload recursion address different levels of the problem. One supplies a finite CTMC computation in a restricted distributional family; the other supplies a broadly applicable limiting representation. Neither alone proves polynomial complexity in the primitive input. This entry now focuses on making the threshold computable with explicit accuracy and runtime bounds. Independent renewal class streams are not silently treated as an iid marked superposition, and critical-load behavior is kept separate.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Use subadditivity, regeneration at all-server jobs, or finite-state descriptions of relative workloads to bound the pile-growth constant. Separate tractability for rational finite-support and phase-type inputs from oracle access to arbitrary distributions.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A numerical stopping rule needs a proved error certificate. Check the iid mark and renewal assumptions, dependence within marks, workload convergence criterion, and the critical equality case separately. An exponential-state exact CTMC is not a polynomial-time result, and two equal successive lower approximations do not certify perfect sampling.

notes_for_maintainer: Reviewed 2026-11-09 against Sections 3-5 of arXiv:2601.20653v1. This is a reported preprint result, not independent certification of every proof. Retargeted the entry from threshold existence to effective computation.

title: Computing the stability threshold of FCFS multiserver-job queues

where_posed.text: The computational question is explicitly identified by Baccelli, Olliaro, Ajmone Marsan, and Marin (2026). The finite-input accuracy formulation here makes that question precise.
where_posed.location: Section 5, immediately after Theorem 5.1 and equation (8).

open_problem: Compute the FCFS saturation growth constant with certified error and explicit complexity bounds for a specified finite input representation. A general threshold representation now exists; compact or polynomial-time evaluation, and critical-load behavior, are separate remaining questions.
